payload.stem: Which computational complexity best characterizes an optimal implementation of Core Algorithms at foundational level?

options.text: O(N log N) using a balanced heap or divide-and-conquer

criteria.name: Complexity Precision
criteria.description: Correctly identifies O(N log N) asymptotic bound.

criteria.name: Algorithmic Justification
criteria.description: Understands tree depth or recurrence relation.

model_answer: Option A is correct: optimal implementations partition the problem space logarithmically, yielding O(N log N) runtime.
explanation: In Core Algorithms, divide-and-conquer structures prune search space effectively, avoiding quadratic time traps.

payload.stem: Fix the subtle boundary or pointer defect in this algorithmic logic for Core Algorithms:
payload.hint: Check loop terminal condition: <= items.length reads past the end of the array.

criteria.name: Index Boundary Fix
criteria.description: Corrects <= to < to avoid accessing undefined.

model_answer: The loop condition `i <= items.length` causes an off-by-one bug reading undefined at `items[items.length]`. Change to `i < items.length`.
explanation: Arrays in JavaScript are zero-indexed with elements from 0 to length - 1. Accessing index length produces undefined.
